evidence_fragments.content: Surgical WAM: A World-Action Model for Data-Efficient Surgical Robot Learning

Wenrui Bao1, Tianyun Jiang, Zhiben Chen, Ser-Nam Lim1, Peter D. Peng2, Yuzhang Shang1∗
1University of Central Florida,2AdventHealth

the termworld–action model(WAM), which we adopt as a
descriptive label for the joint distribution
pθ(ot+1:t+K , at:t+Hc |o ≤t, s≤t, c),(1)

In our surgical setting,ot is the current
endoscopic RGB frame andst the dVRK proprioceptive
state. Our recipe applies to any WAM whose latent sequence
contains both video and action slots processed by a shared
network, so that weights learned without action labels can be
reused for action prediction.

As the backbone used throughout our exper-
iments, we instantiate the WAM with Cosmos Policy (Kim
etal.2026),adiffusion-transformerrealizationofEquation(1)

whose latent sequence contains dedicated slots for past visual
observations, robot state, future predictions, and actions, all
processedbyasinglenetwork.Itsvisualandfuture-prediction
slots are architecturally compatible with action-free video
diffusionbackbones,soweightsobtainedbyaction-freevideo
pretraining transfer directly into Cosmos Policy and serve as
the initialization for the action-labeled stage.

InthisworkweinstantiateStage1withthesurgical
videoworldmodelofHeetal.(2026),obtainedbyfine-tuning
a general video diffusion backbone (Agarwal et al. 2025) on
large-scale surgical video. Its weights populate the visual and
future-predictionslotsoftheWAM,whiletheactionandstate
slots are initialized fresh and learned in Stage 2.

Starting from the
video-pretrained initialization θ0, we fine-tune the full
model on action-labeled surgical demonstrationsDva =
{(o1:T , s1:T , a1:T , c)}. We denote the conditioning context
at timetbyh t := (o≤t, s≤t, c). Each training example pairs
this context with an action chunk and the corresponding
future-prediction targets.

Action
and future-prediction tokens are denoised jointly through the
sameattentionandvisual-predictionparameters.Thiscouples
the action-prediction stream to the temporal structure learned
during video-only pretraining, allowing the model to transfer
video-derived dynamics representations while learning to
predict executable surgical actions.

Although only
actions are sent to the actuator, the model samples the action
and future-prediction tokens jointly: action tokens attend to
the denoised future-prediction tokens at every diffusion step,
preserving at inference the video-action coupling learned
during finetuning. The future-prediction outputs are then dis-
carded, so joint sampling adds compute but no I/O overhead.

At test time the finetuned model is used as a closed-loop
receding-horizon policy. Given the current observation and
task embedding, the diffusion sampler produces an action
chunk of lengthHc together with the corresponding future-
prediction slots; the robot executes the firstHe ≤H c actions,
discards the rest, and the loop then re-observes and re-plans.
Smaller He improves reactivity while largerHe amortizes
the cost of diffusion sampling.

The benchmark provides endoscopic
observations, robot proprioception, and synchronized actions
for simulated dVRK manipulation tasks.
We consider four tasks: Needle Pick, Peg Transfer, Needle
Regrasp, and BiPeg Transfer. Needle Pick and Peg Transfer
are unilateral manipulation tasks, while Needle Regrasp and
BiPegTransferrequirebimanualcoordination.Together,these
tasks involve reaching, grasping, contact-rich manipulation,
object transfer, and precise placement.

To probe whether the benefit of action-free video pretraining
transfers beyond simulation, we apply the identical two-stage
protocol to demonstrations from the JIGSAWS dataset (Gao
et al. 2014), a standard corpus of dVRK operation recordings
captured on real robotic hardware (Figure 3). We observe
the same qualitative trend as in simulation: video-pretrained

scratch baseline.

capability_assessments.rationale: Implemented learned future-scene generation is coupled to an executing policy with simulator decision results. No separate lower-level prediction tests, specified-action query, causal validity, physical execution or clinical assurance are inherited.
The same future-grounded policy mechanism has separately reported simulator control results; lower performance does not remove this functional label.

gate_assessments.rationale: Provenance, versions, pretraining overlap, evaluation boundaries and independent checkpoint selection are insufficiently reported; no observed leakage is inferred.
Implemented state and learned temporal prediction are supported, but no reference-based future-state fidelity evaluation is supplied. L4 cannot replace it.
Future-sequence generation is described, but K, evaluated extent, drift and a tolerance-supported horizon are unreported. Action counts are not evaluated forecast extent.
The scoped evaluated claim is simulator control improvement, not a calibrated probabilistic guarantee or uncertainty-dependent decision. Sampling alone does not activate or pass this gate.

The controller-profile action assessment encounters a scope/dependency mismatch: this joint-output policy lacks an established settable-action prediction query. Command attributes, support and constraints are also incomplete. Applicability of the gate as written requires adjudication, not an invented pass or an executed-test failure.
No modeled scene-intervention-effect estimand or therapeutic-benefit interpretation is evaluated. Attribution of benefit to a training recipe is a different claim.
Future-policy coupling and decision results are supported; exploitation/mismatch stress tests, coverage and acceptance criteria are not.

Selected BP_CONTROLLER research-assurance baseline; proposed surgical control/physical translation requires scoped risk assessment. Guards, abstention and tested fallback are unreported. This is not a clinical authorization requirement or an observed safety failure.
Beyond-simulation claims lack quantitative held-out evaluation, aligned checkpoint/adaptation details and overlap controls.
Teleoperation recordings and an unquantified trend do not establish autonomous physical execution, matched sim-to-real agreement or an actual human model-evaluation task.
The selected use is simulation research, not a live real-care/workflow utility claim.
No defined operational release is assessed; manuscript publication is not operational deployment. Asset-release and governance evidence remain unreported.

legacy_cells.AK: Initialization from the surgical video world model of He et al. (2026).
legacy_cells.AL: Action-free pretraining denoises future-video latents using a video-prediction diffusion loss.
legacy_cells.AM: Shared latent sequence; action and future-prediction tokens are jointly denoised through the same attention and visual-prediction parameters.
legacy_cells.BD: Absolute Cartesian end-effector target; position, orientation, and gripper open–close command per arm; predicted chunk length Hc=16; executes prefix He=4 by default.
legacy_cells.BL: Predicted action chunk Hc=16; default executed prefix He=4 actions before replanning.
